scope: Generic workflow requirements, documented third-party APIs and relative effort/resource classification
rating_status: Analyst classification under each workflow's stated conditions; runtime and memory benchmarks require measured runs.

human_effort_scale.1: Direct parameter entry or import of an identified, correctly scaled asset; little interpretation.
human_effort_scale.2: Limited tracing, cleanup, feature association or assembly placement with explicit inputs.
human_effort_scale.3: Calibration, reconstruction review, moderate remodeling or semantic data preparation.
human_effort_scale.4: Several evidence sources, substantial feature interpretation, articulated assemblies or repeated reconciliation.
human_effort_scale.5: Research reconstruction, ambiguous multi-view interpretation, or a complex combination requiring custom methods.

setup_effort_scale.1: One existing application or executable with explicit inputs.
setup_effort_scale.2: One scriptable library or a documented application scripting setup.
setup_effort_scale.3: Several tools, exchange adapters, component metadata or application-session control.
setup_effort_scale.4: GPU/model environment, sensor calibration or several specialized software stacks.
setup_effort_scale.5: Research code integration or custom reconstruction/semantic adapters.

compute_scale.1: Small CPU parsing, parameter changes, coordinate transforms or lightweight geometry.
compute_scale.2: CPU CAD operations, small assemblies, moderate mesh operations or small image processing.
compute_scale.3: Substantial CPU/RAM use for dense clouds, decomposition, batches or large scenes; optional acceleration.
compute_scale.4: Dense image reconstruction or view-synthesis training with substantial processing, or GPU image-to-3D inference in the chosen route; CPU/GPU support follows the recorded backend.
compute_scale.5: Large-memory GPU models or several heavy reconstruction/training branches in the selected route.

ranking_rules: Rate the complete requested output, including CAD remodeling when that is the recipe goal.
State the input size/quality, output representation and software/backend conditions for the comparison.
Explain lighter/heavier variants, especially image generation versus metric CAD, clean DXF versus raster interpretation, and known assembly versus inferred joints.
Human effort, setup effort and computing demand are independent axes. They are ordinal comparisons, not durations, accuracy scores or measured hardware usage.
Recorded operation counts describe the documented recipe granularity and are not counts of human actions or runtime jobs.
Keep source claims, proposed composition, reference code and actual local verification separate.
